declarations.name: WaterfallTotalsMode
declarations.documentation:
Shared waterfall "totals" semantics, used by every backend template
(Vega-Lite / ECharts / Chart.js) and by the `totals` property `check` so the
options UI and the rendered chart never disagree on the default.

A waterfall bar is either a *delta* (floats off the running cumulative) or a
*total* (anchored at zero, "touches down" to the running cumulative). When
the data has no explicit type column, Flint infers which ends are totals.
The user's `totals` property is purely an *override* of that inference.

members.name: divergingMidpoint
members.documentation:
The value a diverging colour scale should pivot on — what the reader is
being asked to compare against.

This is a judgement, not a fact about the field, which is why it has to
be declared rather than inferred. A temperature in °C pivots at 0 if the
question is whether it freezes, and at something nearer 18 if the
question is whether a city is comfortable to live in; the numbers are
identical either way and only the question tells them apart. Declare it
when the chart is about the comparison — above and below an average, a
target, a baseline period, a comfort line — and leave it out otherwise,
in which case the pivot falls back to whatever the type and the data
make obvious: a sign change at zero, a bounded domain's centre, or no
pivot at all.

Declaring one also *asserts* the split: the scale diverges even if every
reading happens to land on one side of it.

puts it on the high side. Unset ⇒ the semantic type decides (signed measures read as
higher-is-better, temperatures run warm-high).

declarations.name: GapSize
declarations.documentation:
How a group of bars shares its step (G1): the gap between the bars in a group, the space between
groups, and so the bars' width. Both gaps are stated against the bar they sit beside — a share of
its width, or px — so a house says "the bars in a group touch" or "a bar's width between groups"
and the bar takes what is left:

    step = k·bar + (k − 1)·gap + spacing

where `k` is the number of bars in a group. The layout plan and every renderer read the same
answer from here, so the plot planned for the groups is the plot the groups are drawn in.
A gap: a share of a bar's width (`0.1`), or pixels (`"2px"`).

declarations.name: Density
declarations.documentation:
The air around a chart's keys and within its header, in em of the keys' type — so it keeps its
proportion to the text it separates — eased with the plot's size, so a small tile packs a little
closer and a large chart breathes a little more, rather than a fixed 18 px that is nothing on a
large chart and a key row's worth on a small one.

The header — the headline, its deck and any keys above the plot — is grouped by its gaps: keys one
above another stand closest, as one group; the title block stands clearly further over them than
its deck's own leading, so the keys do not read as another line of it; and the block stands
further again from the plot — the theme's title gap, held between a little more and a few times
the title's gap to the keys, so the header neither runs into the plot nor floats off it. A key
with no title above it keeps its own gap to the plot. A theme sets any of them (`legend.gaps`),
and what it sets stands as set.

declarations.name: ZeroClass
declarations.documentation:
Classification of whether zero is a meaningful baseline for a semantic type.

- `meaningful`: 0 has a real-world interpretation (absence of the measured thing).
  Comparisons to zero and ratios between values are meaningful.
  Examples: Count, Revenue, Distance, Weight.

- `arbitrary`: 0 is either meaningless, doesn't exist, or is an arbitrary
  reference point. The data's range is what matters.
  Examples: Temperature (0°F is arbitrary), Year (year 0 doesn't exist),
  Rank (0th place doesn't exist).

- `contextual`: 0 is meaningful but data-fitting may be better when data
  is concentrated far from zero and the mark is not bar/area.
  Examples: Percentage (0–100% natural, but 48–52% benefits from zoom),
  Score (1–5 scale, but 4.2–4.8 benefits from zoom).

declarations.name: ZeroDecision

Result of the zero-baseline decision.
Encapsulates both the boolean decision and domain padding for non-zero axes.

members.name: zero
members.documentation: Whether the axis should include zero

members.name: domainPadFraction
members.documentation:
For non-zero axes: fraction of data range to pad on each side
so edge values aren't crushed against the axis boundary.
e.g. 0.05 = 5% padding on each side.

members.name: zeroClass
members.documentation: The zero class that drove this decision

members.name: forced
members.documentation:
Whether this is a *forced* (non-debatable) decision:
  - `true`  → mandatory: a length/area mark, data that crosses zero, or a
    zero-meaningful type on a length mark. Including zero is structural.
  - `false` → the engine still has a recommended `zero`, but anchoring at
    zero is at least conceptually a choice.
`forced` records the structural side of the decision; it is NOT the gate
for the UI toggle — see `uncertain` below.

members.name: uncertain
members.documentation:
Whether the zero-vs-fit choice is a *genuine toss-up worth surfacing* to
the user. Hosts read this (via the property `check`) to decide whether to
show the "Zero X/Y" toggle at all.

We deliberately keep this narrow to avoid UI clutter: it is `true` ONLY
for a zero-meaningful field on a position mark whose data sits far enough
from zero that anchoring at zero would noticeably compress the view (a
real zoom-in-vs-anchor tradeoff). Every other case — arbitrary types
(zero is meaningless, just fit the data), contextual types (the engine's
data-range call is confident enough), meaningful types whose data already
spans most of the way to zero (the choice barely changes anything), and
all forced/unknown cases — is `false`, so no toggle is shown and the
engine's `zero` value simply applies. The engine's `zero` remains the
recommended default when the toggle is shown.

declarations.name: RuleSpec
declarations.documentation:
A rule the house draws — a gridline, the zero rule, the baseline: a presence, or the presence
with its own style. An object states a drawn rule: without `presence` it is `quiet`.

declarations.name: MinorGridSpec
declarations.documentation: The finer lines between a grid's labelled lines.

declarations.name: SizeToken
declarations.documentation: A design-token size reference (`text.100`, `text.hero900`) or a raw px number.

declarations.name: TypeWeight
declarations.documentation: A named weight, or the CSS number (100–900).

members.name: weight
members.documentation: The full CSS scale: `thin` (100) … `regular` (400) … `black` (900), or the number itself.

members.name: style
members.documentation: Journals set decks and captions in italic; it is a role, not an accident.

members.name: case
members.documentation:
`upper`, `lower`, `title` (each word capitalised, short joining words kept lower-case) or
`sentence` (first letter capitalised, the rest as written). Applied where the text is measured,
so a wider upper-case headline is fitted as it will be drawn.

members.name: lineWeight
members.documentation: Stroke width of the axis rule in px. Presence still decides whether it is drawn.

members.name: color
members.documentation: The rule's and ticks' own ink, in place of `ink.structure.axis`; the presence still tones it (AX1).

members.name: labelGap
members.documentation:
Distance from the axis rule to its labels in px. For outward ticks, the
tick occupies the first part of this distance.

members.name: placement
tickDensity
members.documentation:
How finely a *measure* ruler is graduated: one gradation per 60 / 45 / 30px
of axis, floored at three. A hint — the renderer still rounds to its own
1/2/5/10 step, so a dense ask on a short axis can land on half units.

members.name: suppressWhenValuesPrinted
members.documentation:
Drop the axis entirely when every mark already prints its own value.
The scale is then carried by the numbers, not by a ruler beside them.
Mirrors `legend.suppressWhenValuesPrinted`.

declarations.name: Ramp
declarations.documentation:
Control points of an interpolator — NOT an indexed set.
Length is resolution, not capacity, so `overflow` does not apply.

members.name: neutral
members.documentation: Diverging only: the ink at the pivot.

members.name: endpointsAgainstSurface
members.documentation: Forbid the ramp endpoints colliding with the canvas.

members.name: surface
text
structure
members.documentation: The ink the presence ordinal scales against.

members.name: zero
members.documentation:
The zero line, when the house makes it more than one gridline among
the rest. The Economist strokes zero in its signature red so every
length is read from a line the eye cannot miss. It borrows `rule`
(then `axis`) where the house says nothing, so a house that draws an
ordinary zero needs to state nothing.

members.name: connector
members.documentation:
The stem of a lollipop, the bridge of a dumbbell. It borrows `rule`
where the house says nothing, but the two are not the same job: a
gridline is read *through*, so it sits at the bottom of the ordinal,
while a connector is part of the mark and has to hold its shape at
a hairline's width. A house whose gridlines are already pale has no
room left below them, and states this ink instead.

members.name: series
minContrast
members.documentation:
The least contrast a series ink keeps against the plot surface. A fill below `fill`
(default 1.25:1) is drawn with a 1px edge in a darker shade of its hue; a line below
`stroke` (default 1.6:1) is darkened in its hue until it passes. Inks that pass are
untouched.

members.name: categoricalByCount
members.documentation:
A set written for an exact number of series, keyed by that number (`{ 2: [...], 3: [...] }`).
A chart with that many series takes its set instead of the first inks of `categorical`. A
chart with more series than `categorical` names may also reach a larger set here, the way it
reaches `categoricalExtended`. One series keeps `single`.

members.name: repeat
members.documentation:
Past the last ink, start the palette again instead of folding the rest into the overflow
ink: for houses whose guide says colours repeat after the *n*th series.

members.name: roles
members.type: { other?: string; total?: string; missing?: string }
members.documentation:
Inks for values that play a role, whatever their position: `other` (Other, Others, Rest of
world …), `total` (Total, Grand total) and `missing` (Missing, Unknown, No data, N/A …).
A value with a role takes its ink and no other series in the chart wears it. `other` is
also the overflow ink when the house names none. Colours for particular values (a party,
an asset class) belong to the chart: the field annotation `colors`, which wins over these.

members.name: byMark
members.documentation:
Inks for one family of marks, keyed by mark: `line`, `area`, `bar` (bars and cells),
`arc` (pies and donuts) or `point`. A chart whose series are drawn by one family takes that
family's `single` and `categorical` in place of the general ones; a chart mixing families
(bars with a line) keeps the general set, so a series has one colour throughout.

members.name: ordinal
members.documentation:
The ramp for ordered series (Gold, Silver, Bronze; Strongly agree … Strongly disagree), its
stops listed in the order the categories take them. Unset ⇒ ordered series sample
`sequential`.

members.name: status
members.type: { positive?: string; negative?: string; neutral?: string }

members.name: selection
signed
members.documentation:
How a signed series is coloured. Applies only when the coloured field itself carries
the sign: a continuous colour whose values cross zero, or categories that split by
sign (increase / decrease, regions netting a gain or a loss). A measure on an axis
that dips below zero leaves the series' colour to the ordinal and categorical rules.

members.name: ordered
members.documentation:
A nominal series whose order the chart declares (the field annotation's `sortOrder`):
`ramp` reads it as ordered and samples the ordinal ramp; `categorical` (default) keeps
distinct hues. A sequence Flint infers on its own (months, compass points) is not
declared and keeps distinct hues.

declarations.name: SeriesMarkFamily
declarations.documentation: The families of marks a house can give their own series inks.

members.name: keyTitle
members.documentation:
A key's title ("Population (M)"). It names a field as an axis title does, so unset parts follow
`axisTitle`'s family, slope and ink, at the key labels' size; with neither stated, the labels'
family and the secondary text ink. Its weight is bold, or heavier where `axisTitle` is, lighter
only where this role says so: the weight is what tells a title from its entries. Its `case` is
not applied: the title is the field's name as written.

members.name: kicker
members.documentation: The line above the headline: a figure label (“FIGURE 2”) or a newsroom kicker, from `chart_spec.label`.

members.name: display
members.documentation: The KPI big-number role — data, not chrome.

members.name: axis
categorical
members.documentation: The axis the chart is indexed by, wherever it is drawn.

members.name: measure
members.documentation: The axis values are read off, wherever it is drawn.

members.name: x
members.documentation:
The axis drawn along the bottom or top (x), whatever it carries: its settings override
the role's (AX1). A house that styles its axes by side — a 2px rule along the bottom on
every chart — states it here rather than by role.

members.name: y
members.documentation: The axis drawn up the left or right (y), whatever it carries; overrides the role's.

members.name: floating
members.documentation:
What the axis lines are where the value scale floats — does not start at zero, as a line
or scatter at 45–90 does. `omit`: the line along the floor is a base, and a base there
would claim a zero the chart does not have, so it is not drawn; the value grid marks the
floor where a tick stands, and the line's ticks go with it. `keep`: the lines frame the
window, wherever it starts. `rangeFrame`: the lines span only the data, set off from the
plot (Tufte's range frame), so the frame stays and says where the data runs. Unset, a
house that rules its value axis keeps the frame; one that grids its values instead omits
the line. Bars and areas start at zero, so a floor under them is always a base.
`rangeFrame` is drawn by Vega-Lite only.

members.name: grid
members.documentation:
Gridlines, bound by what the axis *does*, not by what it holds.

`measure` is the grid the reader reads values off — the lines that run
across the value axis. `category` is the grid across the axis the chart
is indexed by, which on a scatter is the horizontal one even though it
carries a number. Houses that rule only horizontally are asking for
`measure` on and `category` off, whatever the two axes happen to hold.

members.name: measure
members.documentation: The grid across the value axis: a presence, or the presence with its own style, dash, weight and ink.

members.name: category
members.documentation: The grid across the axis the chart is indexed by; styled on its own, as `measure`.

members.name: style
members.documentation: The style both grids take unless one states its own.

members.name: dash
members.documentation:
The dash rhythm in px, `[dash, gap]`. `style` only names a family and
picks a default; the length of the dash is its own decision, and a
long dash reads as a guide where a short one reads as a dotted rule.

members.name: weight
members.documentation: Stroke width of visible gridlines in px.

members.name: zero
members.documentation:
A separate rule where the value axis crosses zero. `omit` leaves
zero as an ordinary gridline; anything else draws it in its own
weight, or the weight, dash and ink it states. Only ever drawn when
zero is inside the domain.

members.name: minor
members.documentation: Fainter lines between the labelled ones, on continuous axes. Vega-Lite only.

members.name: layer
members.documentation: `front` draws both grids over the marks (white rules cutting the bars); default `behind`. A grid may state its own. Vega-Lite only.

members.name: frame
members.documentation:
The rule round the plot: a presence, or one with its own weight, dash and ink, so a house
whose frame is as heavy as its grid can say so. Dashes are drawn by Vega-Lite only.

members.name: baseline
members.documentation: The rule the marks stand on (A7): a presence, or one with its own weight, dash and ink.

members.name: group
members.documentation: How a group of bars shares its step (`geometry.band.group`).

members.name: areaEdge
members.documentation: The line along the top of each area (`geometry.area.edge`), in the area's own ink; never an outline on other marks.

members.name: barOpacity
members.documentation: How opaque a bar's fill is (`geometry.band.opacity`), 0–1; areas keep `fillOpacity`.

members.name: barMinLength
members.documentation: The least length, px, of a non-zero bar (`geometry.band.minLength`).

members.name: gradient
members.documentation: Gradient fills: an area that fades to its baseline, a wash under each line.

members.name: cornerRadius
members.documentation:
How far the *value* end of a bar is rounded, in px — the top of a
column, the right of a horizontal bar — and, on a wedge, its corners.
Only the value end of a bar moves; the baseline stays a clean edge, so a
stack still reads as one column. A house that says nothing keeps square
corners; a friendlier, less clinical house rounds them.

members.name: outline
members.documentation:
A stroke drawn around every filled mark — a bar, wedge, or point: the
"sticker" / flat-illustration edge. It is not a `separator` (which cuts
*between* adjacent pieces) nor a `frame` (which bounds the plot): it
bounds each mark on its own, so a lone bar carries it too. A bar's
outline stands down where the bar is too thin to hold it (so a dense bar
chart keeps its fill); a grid cell is a field, held apart by a `tile`
gap, not an outline. Large points keep the outline while dense point
clouds may shrink the whole dot so the border does not turn the plot
into a solid field. `ink` draws it in the house's dark structural ink;
`surface` draws it in the page. A house that says nothing leaves its
marks unbordered.
`series` draws each mark's border in its own series ink, at full strength.

members.name: slice
members.documentation:
A wedge sits in no band, so how far apart neighbouring wedges stand is
its own question. A house may rule its stacked bars with a half-pixel
hairline and still want a clean cut between the pieces of a pie: two
arcs of the same size at different orientations are hard enough to
compare without also having to find where one ends. Where the house
says nothing, wedges are held apart the way its bars are.

`rule` paints the shared edge in the separator's ink, which reads as a
gap of constant width. `pad` swings the wedges apart instead, so the
gap opens at the rim and closes to nothing at the centre.

members.name: arc
members.documentation: Wedge order, start angle and hole (`geometry.arc`).

members.name: tile
members.documentation:
How far apart the cells of a grid stand — a heatmap, a calendar, a
matrix. A cell is not a bar: it has no band to give back, its two
neighbours are on two axes, and its colour is the reading, so a gap
between cells has to be cut out of the shape the way a wedge's is.

Whether to cut at all is a real difference between houses and not a
detail. Flush cells read as a continuous field — the eye follows the
gradient across a row and sees a season. Cut cells read as a table of
separate readings, which is what a house wants when it prints the number
inside each one. Where the house says nothing, cells are held apart the
way its bars are.

The gap is painted, not spaced, and it takes the surface unless the
house asks for structure: on a grid whose colour *is* the value, an edge
in any other ink reads as data.

members.name: point
presence
members.documentation:
Whether a *line* carries a dot at each of its vertices. This is a
question about lines, not about dots: a scatter's dots are drawn
because the chart is a scatter, and no house presence turns them off.

members.name: size
members.documentation:
How big a primary dot this house draws, as an area in px² — the way
the renderer states a point's size and the way the size channel is
read. This covers marks whose point is itself the reading: a scatter,
a dot plot, or the ends of a dumbbell.

Where the house says nothing the renderer's default stands. The
layout remains free to shrink it when the plot runs short of room.

members.name: secondarySize
members.documentation:
How big a supporting vertex is, as an area in px². A radar vertex or
a sampled point on a connected shape confirms the path's position;
it is not the primary mark and must not obscure that path or its
grid. Defaults to the smaller of `size` and 25px².

members.name: opacity
members.documentation: How opaque a dot is, 0–1; unset, the renderer's own.

members.name: ink
members.documentation:
The ink of a line's vertex dots: the series' own ink (the default), the house's text ink
(dark dots on coloured lines), or a colour the house names. A scatter's dots are the
series and always take its ink.

members.name: density
members.documentation:
Which lines keep the dots (M5): `countable` (default) — lines of up to 12 readings; `all` —
every line, the dots shrinking to fit; `sparse` — only where readings stand 20px apart or more.

members.name: halo
members.documentation:
A ring in the plot's surface colour around each dot, so dots that overlap, or sit on a line,
stay countable. A line's dots get one wherever lines can cross unless this says `omit`; a
scatter's dots get one only where it is declared. An `outline` takes its place (a dot has
one stroke). A halo and an opacity below 1 are not combined: ringed dots are solid.

members.name: connector
weight
members.documentation:
The weight of a connector that runs from a mark to the baseline — a
lollipop's stem. It restates nothing: the dot's position already
carries the value and the stem only leads the eye down to the axis,
so it is drawn as structure.

members.name: spanWeight
members.documentation:
The weight of a connector that runs between two marks — a dumbbell's
bridge. This one is not redundant: the *distance* it draws is the
reading, and a hairline asks the eye to measure a gap it can barely
see. It keeps structure's ink and takes a mark's weight.

Where the house says nothing, a bridge is drawn at the weight the
house gives its lines: it is a mark, so it takes a mark's weight.

members.name: summary
reference
members.type: { presence?: Presence; style?: 'tick' | 'line' | 'dashed'; weight?: number; label?: boolean }

members.name: texture
members.type: { pattern?: 'vary' | 'hatch'; patterns?: TexturePattern[]; ink?: 'darker' | 'white'; spacing?: number }
members.documentation:
How the `texture` channel is drawn on filled marks (bars, wedges, areas): `vary` (default)
gives each series its own pattern — diagonal, the other diagonal, horizontal, vertical, cross,
dots — so series differ without colour; `hatch` gives every series the same diagonal hatch in
its own ink. `patterns` names the house's own sequence instead, in palette order (`solid`
leaves that series a flat fill). The lines are a darker shade of the fill (`ink: "darker"`) or white.

declarations.name: PointShape
declarations.documentation:
The glyph a house draws a dot as — a scatter's points, a line's vertices, a dumbbell's ends —
wherever the chart does not encode shape itself. Where it does, the house's shape is the first
the shape scale hands out. Unset, a dot is a circle.

declarations.name: TexturePattern
declarations.documentation: A fill pattern the texture channel draws; `solid` is a plain fill in the series ink.

declarations.name: LabelFitStep
declarations.documentation: A step category names may take when they do not fit their band (`labels.overflow`).

declarations.name: ThemeLabelFit
declarations.documentation: The thresholds category names are set against (`labels.fit`).

members.name: minChars
members.documentation: Characters a cut name keeps before its ellipsis; a cut that keeps fewer is not taken. Default 4.

members.name: turnedLimit
members.documentation: The widest a turned name runs before it is cut: px, or a share of the plot's height (`"40%"`, the default).

members.name: gap
members.documentation: Space two straight names keep between them, in em. Default half an em, at least 6px.

members.name: rowLimit
members.documentation: The widest a row name down y runs before it wraps or is cut: px, or a share of the chart's width. Default a quarter of it, at least 180px.

members.name: rowNames
members.documentation:
Where the names of horizontal bars stand. `beside` (the default): down the y axis, left of the
bars. `above`: each on its own line over its bar, the full width of the chart theirs — the
bands take twice their room, by the same stretch, and where the canvas cannot hold that the
names stand beside. `auto`: above only where, beside, a name would be cut or wrapped. One bar
to a band only: grouped bars and small multiples keep their names beside.

members.name: overflow
members.documentation:
The path category names along x take when they do not stand flat and whole. Names that fit
are always flat — a theme never forces a turn. Leave it unset for the general path:
- a row of names: `["wrap", "rotate90"]`;
- a sequence that explains itself (times, dates, months, years, decades, ranks, by semantic
  type): `["wrap", "skip", "rotate90"]`.
Add `"rotate45"` before `"rotate90"` where the house turns labels 45°. Steps: `wrap` (two
lines, or one in wider bands), `skip` (only the round values, sequences only), `rotate45`,
`rotate90`. Trimming is not a step: any step may trim its names (an ellipsis at the band or
at `fit.turnedLimit`) unless `truncation` is `"never"`. The path's order binds; within it,
every step is weighed at every size down to the floor and the cheapest taken. A chart can
state its own path in `chartProperties.labelOverflow`.

members.name: fit
members.documentation: The thresholds the names are set against; each has a default.

members.name: title
members.documentation:
Whether a key carries its field's name. `always`; or `whenAmbiguous` (the default), which
leaves it off only on proof the reader does not need it: the headline, deck or an axis on the
same field already names it, the chart makes the key itself, or every value proves one closed
kind (months, years, countries…) under a field name that says no more. A semantic type is not
proof. An author who wants no title says so on the encoding. `omit` is read as `whenAmbiguous`.

members.name: maxSwatches
members.documentation:
The most entries a key to *values* may spend. A legend that names ten
bubble sizes is a table, not a key. Unset, a size key lists round values
as its edge has room for — one for every 80 px of the plot's side it
stands on, from three to five — each symbol clearly larger than the last.

members.name: swatch
members.documentation:
The symbol beside each name in a key to categories: `auto` (default) takes it from the mark —
a square for bars, a stroke for lines, the dot's own shape for points; `square`, `circle` or
`line` (a short stroke) draw that symbol for every mark. A key whose entries are shapes (a
shape channel) or sizes keeps its own symbols. Vega-Lite only.

members.name: arrangement
members.documentation: Several keys above or below the plot: side by side, or one above another. A preference: it gives way where the keys would overflow.

members.name: titlePosition
members.documentation: A key's title above its entries, or before them on their line, above or below the plot. A preference.

members.name: align
members.documentation: Where keys stand along their edge: from its start, centred, at its end, or spread across it.

members.name: gaps
members.type: { title?: number; stack?: number; row?: number; plot?: number }
members.documentation:
The air around keys, in em of their labels — so it keeps its proportion to the type — and
eased smoothly with the plot's size (0.7 on a small tile to 1.3 on a large chart).
`title`: the title block to keys standing under it; `stack`: between keys one above another;
`row`: between keys side by side, and keys one above another beside the plot; `plot`: a key to
the plot. Unset: the header grouped by its gaps — 0.6 em for `stack`, an em for `title`, 2.25 em
for `row`; an em for `plot`, by `layout.density`.

members.name: suppressWhenAxisNames
members.documentation: The legend restates the categorical axis — delete it.

members.name: suppressWhenValuesPrinted
members.documentation: The legend restates a number already printed in every mark — delete it.

members.name: endValue
members.documentation:
Names at the line ends also say where each line ends — "Japan 84.5" — in the value labels'
number format. They follow the rows the chart draws, so a chart whose rows are replaced
(re-indexed, filtered) keeps its names honest.

members.name: anchor
members.documentation:
Where a label printed inside a bar sits along it: at the value `end` (default), at the bar's
`start` (its base, so the numbers read as one column), or in the `middle`.

members.name: fallback
members.documentation:
When some bars are too short to hold their label inside: `perMark` (default) prints just those
past their end; `allOutside` prints every label past its bar's end, so they read alike.

members.name: minContrast
members.documentation: The contrast (x:1) a label printed on a mark keeps with it under `contrastWithMark`; default 3.

members.name: axisTitles
members.documentation:
`whenAmbiguous` asks the same question of each axis: `Jan Feb Mar` names
its own kind and needs no title over it, `26 20 14` names nothing until
one is written. Ranks and binned ranges count as numbers.
`omit` moves required titles and declared units to the end of the
subtitle rather than relying on the author's prose to name the axes.

members.name: axisTitlePlacement
members.documentation:
Where a still-needed axis title sits. `flatAboveAxis` lays it straight
at the head of its own ruler, beside the values it names.

members.name: axisTitleGap
members.documentation:
Distance in px from an axis title to the plot-side edge it labels.
Realization maps this to native title padding or, for a flat y title,
to its offset above the plot.

members.name: numberFormat
compact
members.documentation:
Number compaction (1,250,000 → 1.25M). The theme says whether, how and where; the field
says whether it may be — by its semantic type (`types`) and its unit (a value already in
millions, `Population (m)`, is never compacted again). Unset, `thousands: "suffix"`
compacts value labels value by value, as before; otherwise nothing is compacted.

members.name: show
members.documentation: `auto` (the default once `compact` is stated) compacts where the largest value reaches `threshold`.

members.name: style
members.documentation: `short` k/M/B/T (default), `upper` K/M/B/T (BI), `lower` k/m/b/t, `editorial` k/m/bn/tn, `si` k/M/G/T.

members.name: per
members.documentation: `scale` (default): one unit for a whole ruler or label set, from its largest value; `value`: each its own.

members.name: threshold
members.documentation: The least largest value that is compacted. Default 10,000.

members.name: on
members.documentation: Where: measure-axis ticks, value labels, or both (default). Tooltips always print the full value.

members.name: types
members.documentation: The semantic types (or families) compacted. Default Amount, Price, Profit, Count, Number, Quantity.

declarations.name: FurnitureZone
FurnitureFrame

members.name: kind
members.documentation:
`rule` — a line across its frame; `band` — a filled strip across its frame; `tab` — a short
block (the Economist's red tab); `text` — a wordmark or credit; `image` — a logo, from inline
`svg` or an image `src`. `mastheadTab`, `headerRule` and `footerRule` are the earlier names:
a tab above the title at the content's start, a rule below the title across the block, and a
rule below the plot.

members.name: at
members.documentation: Where it sits. Defaults: `canvasTop` for rules, bands and tabs; `aboveTitle` for text and images.

members.name: frame
members.documentation: What it is aligned to or spans. Defaults: `canvas` for a rule or band on the edge, else `content`.

members.name: align
members.documentation: Which end of its frame it sits at. Default `start`. Rules and bands span the frame.

members.name: anchor
members.documentation: The earlier corner placement, read by `mastheadTab`, `headerRule` and `footerRule`.

members.name: width
members.documentation: px. A tab's or image's width; a rule or band spans its frame unless given one.

members.name: height
members.documentation: px. A rule's weight, a band's or tab's or image's height.

members.name: text
members.documentation: The words of a `text` item, set in `type` (else the deck's type).

members.name: svg
members.documentation: Inline SVG markup for an `image` item.

members.name: src
members.documentation: An image URL or data URI for an `image` item.

members.name: href
members.documentation: Where the item links to, when it is clicked.

members.name: alt
members.documentation: The image's text alternative.

declarations.name: ThemeSource
declarations.documentation:
The source line (S1). The chart says what the source is (`chart_spec.source`); the house says how
it reads: a lead-in, where it sits, a rule above it, a credit of its own. Set in `type.footnote`.

members.name: show
members.documentation: `whenGiven` (default) draws the chart's source; `never` leaves it to the host page.

members.name: leadIn
members.documentation: The words before the source; default `"Source:"`, `""` for none.

members.name: leadInWeight
members.documentation: The lead-in's weight, slope and case, where they differ from the source's.

members.name: align
members.documentation: Which end of the frame the line sits at; default `start`.

members.name: frame
members.documentation: `content` (default): inside the margin, with the headline; `canvas`: the graphic's outer edges.

members.name: rule
members.type: { presence?: Presence; width?: number; color?: string; dash?: number[] }
members.documentation: A rule across the frame above the source line.

members.name: credit
members.documentation:
The house's own credit: `inline` after the source (with `separator`), at the frame's other
`end`, or on the `nextLine`.

members.name: image
members.type: { svg?: string; src?: string; width: number; height: number }
members.documentation:
A logo in place of the credit's words, at the frame's other end, level with the source
(`placement: "end"` only; `text` stays its alternative text): inline `svg` or a `src` URL
or data URI (PNG works), drawn `width`×`height` px.

members.name: gap
members.documentation: px between the chart and the source line (or its rule); default 8.

members.name: density
members.documentation:
Air around the plot: the canvas padding, and a key's gap to the plot (0.8, 1 or 1.4 em of its
labels, unless `legend.gaps.plot` says). Not the ruler's gradations — those are `tickDensity`.

members.name: titleBlock
position
members.documentation: Place the semantic title above the chart or as a caption below it.

members.name: gap
members.documentation:
The vertical gap between the title block and the chart below it — a
house's whitespace personality reaching the headline. `tight` packs
the chart up under the title (a dense figure, a dashboard tile);
`loose` gives an action title room to breathe (a slide exhibit). Keys above the plot join
the block: the title stands an em over them (`legend.gaps.title`), and this gap
stands below them.

members.name: deckGap
members.documentation: The vertical gap between the headline and its deck (subtitle).

members.name: frame
members.documentation:
The edge the title block starts from: `content` (default) — the canvas inside its margin,
past the category labels; `plot` — the plot's own left edge, so the headline lines up with
the start of the x axis.

members.name: bandStepFit
members.documentation:
How strongly category pitch follows the available discrete-axis span.
  On sparse one-banded axes, `0` preserves `bandStep`, `1` fills the span,
  and intermediate values linearly blend the two. Under pressure normal
  elasticity applies to `bandStep`. A grid's cells (both axes banded) are not bars: they keep
  their reading target, and grow past it toward the size that fills the base by this share, to
  twice the target at most.

declarations.name: ThemeGuard
declarations.documentation: A predicate over signals the compiler already resolves. Deliberately closed.

members.name: then
members.documentation: Policy blocks only — `ink` and `type` may not vary.

members.name: because
members.documentation: Required: a variant without a stated reason is an inconsistency.

declarations.name: GeometryKind
declarations.documentation:
The geometries a chart can be built out of, named by what the reader does
with the shape rather than by the renderer's mark.

`band` and `cell` are the reason this list exists and is not just a list of
mark types: Vega-Lite draws both with `rect`, but a bar in a row and a tile
in a grid take opposite answers to the same question. A gap between bars is
rhythm; a gap between cells cuts a continuous field into a table.

members.name: wash
members.documentation:
A wash under each line, down to the baseline, in the line's own ink: `tint` is a flat pale
fill, `fade` runs from the ink at the line to clear at the baseline. Default `none`.

members.name: washOpacity
members.documentation: How strong the wash is where it meets the line, 0–1 (default 0.12 for `tint`, 0.3 for `fade`).

members.name: presence
members.documentation: Whether a line carries a dot at each reading. A scatter's dots are the chart, not this.

members.name: size
members.documentation: Area in px², the way both the renderer and the size channel state a dot.

members.name: shape
members.documentation: The glyph every dot is drawn as: `circle` (default), `square`, `diamond`, `triangle` or `cross`.

members.name: opacity
members.documentation:
How opaque a dot is, 0–1. Unset, the renderer's own: Vega-Lite draws a scatter's dots at 0.7
so overlaps show through. A house whose marks are flat planes states 1. Dots a full plot shrinks
rise toward solid, holding diameter × opacity. A chart's own
`opacity` property still wins.

members.name: ink
members.documentation: The ink of a line's vertex dots: `series` (default), `text`, or a colour.

members.name: halo
members.documentation:
A ring in the plot's colour around each dot, so overlapping dots stay countable. A line's dots
get one wherever lines can cross unless this says `omit`; a scatter's dots only where it is
declared. A quarter of the dot's radius, at most `width`; a scatter's dots under 28px² get
none. An outline takes its place. Not combined with an `opacity` below 1: ringed dots are solid.

members.name: density
members.documentation:
Which lines keep the dots (M5): `countable` (default) — lines of up to 12 readings; `all` —
every line, the dots shrinking to fit; `sparse` — only where readings stand 20px apart or more.

members.name: edge
members.documentation: The line along the top of the fill: an area that keeps its edge reads as a line with a wash.

members.name: fill
members.documentation:
`fade` runs the fill from the area's ink at its top to clear at the baseline. Stacked bands
keep a solid fill: each sits on the next, and a fade would melt one into the other.

members.name: fraction
members.documentation: How much of its step the bar fills, 0–1. The rest is the gap.

members.name: group
members.documentation:
Grouped (dodged) bars: `gap` between the bars in a group and `spacing` between groups, each a
share of a bar's width (`0` touching, `1` a bar's width) or px (`"2px"`); the bars take what is
left of the step: the bar's width is derived, and the step is a guideline. Unset `spacing`
keeps `fraction` for the group as a whole, but never less than half a bar or three gaps, so
groups read as groups; unset `gap` is a twentieth of a bar, at least 1px.

members.name: cornerRadius
members.documentation: Rounding at the *value* end only, so a stack still reads as one column.

members.name: outlineInk
members.documentation: The ink of the outline: the structure ink (default), the surface, or each bar's own series ink.

members.name: minLength
members.documentation:
The least length, px, a bar with a non-zero value is drawn (M6): a near-zero bar shows as a
stub at the baseline rather than vanishing into it. Zero stays empty.

members.name: gap
members.documentation: How far neighbouring wedges stand apart, in px.

members.name: gapStyle
members.documentation: `rule` paints the shared edge; `pad` swings the wedges apart.

members.name: order
members.documentation:
The order wedges run clockwise from the start (M4): the data's order (default), or largest
first. A chart that sorts its own slices keeps its sort.

members.name: startAngle
members.documentation: Where the first wedge starts, in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock (default 0).

members.name: hole
members.documentation: The hole as a share of the outer radius, 0–0.9, for every donut the house draws.

members.name: gap
members.documentation: Cut between tiles, in px. Zero keeps the grid a continuous field.

declarations.name: ThemeGeometry
declarations.documentation:
Geometry the house states once and every chart built from that shape reads.

Measured against the theme lab: `line.width`, `point.presence` and
`point.size` all split inside a replicated cluster — one chart, many
languages, different answers — so they are house decisions and belong here.
`point.fill` did not split, which is why nothing here asks a house to state it.

There is deliberately no per-chart-type sibling to this block. The lab was
asked for one and refused: of the twelve (house, chart type) groups holding
more than one chart, eight disagree with themselves, so a rule keyed by chart
type could not have carried them anyway. What the disagreements track is
series count and faceting — NYT, the Economist and Power BI all thin their
line to exactly 2px for the four-series chart and run 2.2–2.5px for a lone
one, and Power BI drops its dots only on the sixteen-panel facet. Those are
`variants`, over signals the compiler already resolves, and a variant may
carry a `geometry` block.

declarations.name: ThemeChartDefaults
declarations.documentation:
The one block that is allowed to name a chart type.

Everything else at level 1 is a policy the compiler binds to whatever chart
it is handed. This is different in kind: it is the house's list of settings
for charts it has an opinion about — the Times puts a dot on every reading
of a line, and a bump chart it prints is never smoothed. Those are not
consequences of a design language, they are house rules, and there is no
honest way to derive them from ink and type.

Keyed by chart type id, or `*` for every chart. Values are chart-property
keys the template already declares. It is a *default*: anything the caller
set explicitly wins, and a key the template does not offer is reported and
dropped. So is a key that changes how the data is read rather than how the
chart looks: axis type, zero baseline, log scale, transform, encoding actions.

declarations.name: ThemeCompileDefaults
declarations.documentation:
Compiler settings the house prefers — the size it draws at, how far a chart
may stretch, how much air a facet gets. These are not style: they decide how
much room the chart has before a single colour is chosen, which is why they
cannot be applied after the fact like ink.

Three levels, in order: what the caller put in the chart spec, then this,
then flint's own defaults. A house sets the middle one.

members.name: selectionBoundary
members.documentation: Paint for the exterior of a contiguous semantic selection.

members.name: haloWidth
members.documentation: Set to zero to disable the contrast halo.

declarations.name: ThemeSpec
declarations.documentation:
Level 1. One JSON document per design language.

Every field is optional, including the ink and the type. A house that states
nothing is not an error — it is the neutral house, and grounding it yields
Flint's own defaults. That matters beyond tidiness: it is what lets the
compiler reason about a chart's design (can it carry value labels? at this
density?) when the caller named no house at all, without having to invent a
second, parallel set of rules for the untheme'd case.

members.name: extends
members.documentation:
Start from a theme Flint ships, then override only the fields this
specification states. Nested objects merge; arrays and scalar values
replace the preset value.

members.name: source
members.documentation: How a chart's source line is drawn, when the chart gives one (`chart_spec.source`).

declarations.name: ThemePreset
declarations.documentation:
A house Flint ships, ready to name by id: `theme_spec: 'economist'`.

Three parts, and they answer different questions. `spec` is what the
compiler reads. `description` is how a caller chooses between houses.
`guidance` is the house talking upstream.

That last one needs saying, because the boundary is easy to blur. A theme
governs the visual: ink, type, furniture, spacing. It does not choose the
fields, the aggregation or the sort — the chart spec does, and it is written
first. So where a house depends on something only the spec can give, it says
so: which words it needs written, which annotations it reads, how many
categories its colour can name. Facts and requests, not instructions — what
to do about a tail of thirty categories is the author's call, and a house
that starts prescribing transformations is overreaching. Hence a few lines.

members.name: description
members.documentation: One line: what this house is for.

members.name: guidance
members.documentation: A few markdown bullets: what this house needs the chart spec to do.

members.name: icon
members.documentation: A 16px SVG standing in for the house in a picker, as a complete document so a caller can drop it straight into an `` or inline it. It is drawn from the house's own decisions rather than invented: the tile is its canvas, the bars are the first three of its categorical set, and the one thing left over says what the house does that the others do not — the Economist's red tab, Swiss's structural black rules, McKinsey's horizontal bars, Nature's bare axis, cartoon's rounded tops. At this size that is all a reader can take in, and it is enough to recognise the house once they have seen one chart in it.

declarations.name: ThemeReport
declarations.documentation:
A downgrade or approximation. Silent fallbacks are indistinguishable from
bugs, so every one of these is surfaced on `spec._theme.report`.
Where a chart departs from what its theme or author stated, or where a stated option cannot apply
to this chart, and why. A setting applied as stated is not reported.

members.name: path
members.documentation: Dotted ThemeSpec path this concerns, e.g. `legend.placement`.

members.name: code
members.documentation: What kind of departure, in kebab case, e.g. `straight-refused`: stable for code and tests to read.

declarations.name: ReportDeparture
declarations.documentation: Records a departure: the ThemeSpec path it concerns, its code, and a message saying why.
declarations.type: (path: string, code: string, message: string) => void

members.name: rule
members.type: { width: number; color: string; dash?: number[] }

members.name: credit
members.type: { text: string; placement: 'inline' | 'end' | 'nextLine'; separator: string; weight?: 'normal' | 'bold' | number; image?: { src: string; width: number; height: number } }

members.name: image
members.type: { src: string; width: number; height: number }

members.name: textCase
members.documentation: The case the role asks for; unset when the text is drawn as written.

declarations.name: ResolvedAxis
declarations.documentation: One axis, already bound to a screen channel.

members.name: orient
members.documentation: `top`/`bottom` for x, `left`/`right` for y.

members.name: label
members.type: ResolvedText & { show?: boolean; limit?: number; padding: number; flush?: boolean; angle?: number; overflow?: LabelFitStep[]; ordered?: boolean }

members.name: title
tickCount
members.documentation: Preferred tick count; undefined = let the renderer choose.

members.name: tickSpacing
members.documentation: The px between labels a measure axis is graduated at.

members.name: tickLabels
members.documentation:
Which ticks carry a label. `all` leaves the choice to the renderer's own
scale; the rest ask for the values the data actually holds, thinned or
cut to the two ends.

members.name: indexing
members.documentation: True when this axis carries what the reader indexes the chart by.

members.name: zeroRule
members.documentation: A rule at zero, drawn only where the value axis crosses it.

members.name: unit
members.documentation: Suffix/prefix policy for the measure this axis carries.

members.name: compact
members.documentation: How the ticks of a measure the theme compacts are shortened; the unit is chosen from the ticks.

members.name: minorGrid
members.documentation: Fainter lines between the labelled gridlines, where this axis's grid carries them.

members.name: gridFront
members.documentation: The grid drawn over the marks rather than behind them.

members.name: categoricalText
members.documentation: The house's text variants, parallel to the categorical tiers.

members.name: visibility
members.type: { stroke: Record<string, string>; outline: Record<string, string> }
members.documentation:
Series inks too faint against the plot surface, and what is drawn instead: `stroke` is the
darker ink a line takes, `outline` the edge a filled mark gains. Keyed by lower-case ink.

members.name: byValue
members.documentation:
Inks bound to the values present in this chart — the chart's own colours, else the house's role
inks — keyed by the value trimmed and lower-cased.

members.name: exhausted
members.documentation:
The data needs more inks than the house named, and the house named no
overflow ink either. Colour can no longer tell the series apart, so the
house set is not imposed — what is on the chart already was chosen for
the count.

members.name: status
members.type: { positive?: string; negative?: string; neutral?: string }

members.name: signedStatus
members.documentation:
One series of bars whose measure crosses zero, in a house that colours signed values by
status: each bar takes `status.positive` or `status.negative` by the sign of its own value.

members.name: range
members.documentation: Concrete range to hand a continuous colour scale (already sampled).

members.name: quantize
members.documentation: Set when the ramp is consumed as discrete bands.

members.name: placement
members.documentation: The placement that actually survived grounding.

members.name: fallbacks
members.documentation:
The rest of the house's ranked list, after the one that survived.

Grounding cannot see everything: whether a name fits inside the band it
names is a question of pixels and text, and it is answered in realize.
When the answer comes back no, the house has already said what it would
rather have — so the fallback is read from here rather than invented.

members.name: titlePolicy
members.documentation: Whether the house titles every key, or only those whose labels do not say what they are.

members.name: titleText
members.documentation: How a key's title is set: the house's `type.keyTitle`, else the labels' face in bold and the secondary ink.

members.name: maxSwatches
members.documentation: The most entries a key to values may spend.

members.name: swatch
members.documentation: A symbol the house states for every entry of a key to categories; unset, the mark's own.

members.name: arrangement
members.documentation: How several keys stand, as the theme prefers; unset leaves it to the plan.

members.name: endValue
members.documentation: Series-end names carry the series' last value.

members.name: anchor
members.documentation: Where an inside label sits along its bar.

members.name: format
members.documentation: d3-format string derived from `annotation.numberFormat` + channel semantics.

members.name: compact
members.documentation: How the labels are compacted, where the theme compacts them; `format` stays the fallback.

members.name: unit
members.documentation:
The unit each printed value carries: a compact unit the field declares
(`%`, `$`, `°C`) unless the format already writes it, else `%` on
part-to-whole values that sum to 100.

members.name: insideMinValue
members.documentation:
Below this magnitude the mark is shorter than its own label, so an
inside label would overrun it. Grounding owns this because it is a
question about space, not about style.

members.name: segmentMinShare
members.documentation:
The smallest share of the measure axis a stacked segment may occupy and
still be labelled — a line of text over the plot's extent along that
axis. Segments below it get no number: it would not fit between the
segment's edges and would read as its neighbour's.

A share rather than a value because the two stack modes divide by
different totals — the tallest stack when the bars are summed, each
bar's own total when they are normalized. Grounding owns it because
only grounding knows the plot's size; by the time a spec is assembled
the height may be a step or a container, not a number.

members.name: segmentMinValue
members.documentation:
`segmentMinShare` as a value on a summed stack: the share of the tallest
stack. Absent on a normalized stack, whose segments divide by their own
bar's total.

members.name: bandNeed
members.documentation:
The band step (px, along the categorical axis, per group where bars are grouped) the labels
need where the band is too narrow for them; the plan widens into the canvas's spare room (L3).

members.name: liveSignal
members.documentation:
The signal a live layout re-plans the labels through. Set when the
visible rows can change after compile: the label layer is built even
where these rows do not print it, and the signal decides whether it shows.

members.name: possible
members.documentation:
Whether this chart could carry value labels *at all* — structurally
labelable, and not so dense that the numbers would be unreadable however
firmly they were asked for.

`show` is what the house decided; this is what the chart permits. A host
reads it to know whether offering the reader a labels control is
meaningful: where it is false the control can do nothing, so it is not
shown rather than shown broken.

members.name: group
members.documentation: How grouped bars share their step.

members.name: gradient
members.documentation: Set only when the house asks for one.

members.name: cornerRadius
members.documentation: Corner radius for the value end of a bar, and a wedge's corners, in px.

members.name: outline
members.type: { color: string; width: number; series?: boolean }
members.documentation: A stroke around each filled bar/wedge/point: the sticker edge (thin bars skip it). `series`: in each mark's own ink.

members.name: barOpacity
members.documentation: How opaque a bar's fill is, where the house says.

members.name: barMinLength
members.documentation: The least length, px, of a non-zero bar.

members.name: areaEdge
members.documentation: The line along the top of each area, in its own ink (stacked bands included).

members.name: point
vertexSize
members.documentation: Set only where the house sized path vertices apart from its primary dots.

members.name: shape
members.documentation: Set only where the house named a glyph other than the circle.

members.name: opacity
members.documentation: Set only where the house stated how opaque its dots are.

members.name: ink
members.documentation: A fixed ink for a line's vertex dots; unset, they take the series' ink.

members.name: density
members.documentation: Which lines keep their dots.

members.name: haloDots
members.documentation: Set where the house declared a halo: standalone dots (a scatter's) carry it too, not only a line's.

members.name: sizeRange
members.documentation: The area a sized mark may take, smallest to largest, in px².

members.name: minSize
members.documentation: The area below which a sized mark stops being a mark.

members.name: observations
members.documentation: Whether the rows behind a summary mark are drawn alongside it.

members.name: separator
members.type: { show: boolean; color: string; width: number }

members.name: slice
members.documentation: How far apart neighbouring wedges of a pie or donut stand, in px.

members.name: arc
members.documentation: Wedge order, start angle and hole, where the house says.

members.name: tile
members.documentation: How far apart the cells of a heatmap or matrix stand, in px.

members.name: connector
members.type: { show: boolean; color?: string; width: number; spanWidth: number; dash?: number[] }
members.documentation:
`width` is the stem — a connector to the baseline. `spanWidth` is the
bridge — a connector between two marks, which draws a distance that is
itself the reading. Both are painted in `color`.

members.name: summary
members.type: { fill: boolean; outline: boolean; centralRule: boolean; widthFraction?: number }

members.name: reference
members.type: { show: boolean; width: number; style?: string; label: boolean }

members.name: redundant
members.documentation:
The redundant channels grounding decided this chart actually gets, after
weighing `redundantEncoding` against how hard the series are to tell
apart by colour alone.

members.name: texture
members.documentation: Pattern fills on filled marks, when the house asks for the texture channel.

declarations.name: DesignDecisions
declarations.documentation: Level 2 output. Backend-neutral, but every role is bound to this chart.

members.name: surface
members.type: { canvas: string; plot?: string; panel?: string }

members.name: text
members.type: { primary: string; secondary: string; muted: string; inverse: string }
members.documentation: Default text ink, for anything not otherwise specified.

members.name: font
members.documentation: Base font family for the chart body.

members.name: title
kicker
members.documentation: The figure label or kicker above the headline.

members.name: frame
members.documentation: The edge the title block starts from.

members.name: offset
members.documentation: Gap from the title block to the chart, in px.

members.name: deckPadding
members.documentation: Gap between the headline and its deck, in px.

members.name: axes
members.documentation: Bound axes, keyed by screen channel.

members.name: baseline
members.documentation:
The rule the marks stand on. `anyFloor`: the house states it strongly — emphasised, or with
its own ink or weight — so it is drawn along the axis's floor even where that is not zero.

members.name: floating
members.documentation: What the axis lines are where the value scale floats (`structure.axis.floating`); unset, inferred from the axes.

members.name: pointEmphasis
members.documentation:
Which points on a line the house dots, and whether it writes the value
there. Only meaningful where the chart draws a line through its data —
stage 3 knows that, stage 2 does not.

members.name: interaction
continuousColorFocus
selectionBoundary
facets
layout
members.documentation: Plot dimensions and step are what layout settled, so realization can test whether annotations fit.

members.name: canvasWidth
members.documentation: The graphic the caller asked for. Wider than `plotWidth` by the axis gutter.

members.name: statistics
members.documentation:
What the house prints alongside a fit: the quantities it expects to see
stated, and where. Only meaningful where the chart actually fits
something — stage 3 knows that, stage 2 does not.

members.name: display
members.documentation: The KPI's big number, when the house states the display role; its size stays fitted to the tile.

members.name: table
members.type: { header: ResolvedText; cell: ResolvedText; headerRule: string; rule: string }
members.documentation:
A chart read as a table: headings in the axis-title role and cells in the axis-label role at
the theme's own sizes, since a table takes the room it needs, and the rules under the
headings and between rows.

members.name: source
members.documentation: How a source line is drawn, when the chart gives one.

members.name: bound
members.documentation: Chart facts stage 3 is allowed to consult (it may not re-derive them).

members.name: seriesField
members.documentation: The field the series is keyed on, and the one the categorical axis names.

members.name: markChannel
members.documentation: The mark family, for realizers that must fake a missing primitive.

declarations.name: TitleMeasure
declarations.documentation: The width of a string in px at a font size, in the font the text is set in.

declarations.name: TitlePlan
declarations.documentation: How a single-view chart's title is fitted to the block it sits over.

members.name: block
members.documentation: The width the title is fitted to: the plot, the category labels beside it, or the canvas.

members.name: headline
members.documentation: The headline, set down a size or broken over lines.

members.name: deck
members.documentation: The deck the theme writes: the author's, then the axis titles it moves there.

members.name: deckFit
members.documentation: The deck broken over lines.

members.name: shift
members.documentation:
How far, in px, a title centred over the plot is moved along it so it stays within the drawing:
the nearest place to centred where it adds no width to the drawing. Unset where it is centred.

members.name: axisTitles
members.documentation: The title each axis prints.

members.name: title
members.documentation: The author's headline and deck.

members.name: rowFacet
members.documentation: The field the rows are faceted by, if any.

members.name: themed
members.documentation: Whether a theme is applied, so it moves axis titles to the deck where it keeps them there.

members.name: viewsWidth
members.documentation: The width the views of a chart of several views span, which its title sits over in place of one plot.

members.name: beside
members.documentation: The width header pieces take beside the headline, at its start and end.

members.name: keysBeside
members.documentation:
The width keys beside the plot take, with their offset: the title spans the whole drawing, so
it may run over them. Rules and the source close only the chart block, and do not.

declarations.name: VisCategory
declarations.documentation:
=============================================================================
TYPE REGISTRY — Single Source of Truth
=============================================================================

Every recognized semantic type is registered here with its orthogonal
compilation dimensions. This is the ONLY place where per-type properties
are defined. All other files (field-semantics.ts, semantic-types.ts)
derive helper functions by querying this registry.

To add a new semantic type: add an entry here.
To query a type's properties: use `getRegistryEntry()`.
=============================================================================

declarations.name: T0Family
declarations.documentation: Top-level type family

declarations.name: T1Category
declarations.documentation: Mid-level category within a family

declarations.name: ZeroBaseline
declarations.documentation:
Zero-baseline classification for quantitative axes.

- `meaningful`: 0 = absence of the measured thing; axis should include 0 (Count, Revenue).
- `arbitrary`:  0 is arbitrary or nonexistent; data-fit the axis (Temperature, Year, Rank).
- `contextual`: 0 is meaningful but data-fitting may be better when data is far from 0 (Percentage, Score).
- `none`:       Not a quantitative type; zero question is irrelevant (all categorical/temporal types).

members.name: zeroBaseline
members.documentation: Zero-baseline classification for quantitative axes

members.name: zeroPad
members.documentation: Domain padding fraction for non-zero axes (0 = no padding)

declarations.name: ChartEncoding
declarations.documentation:
Encoding definition for a single channel, using field names directly.
This is the library-level encoding — no fieldID indirection.

members.name: scheme
members.documentation:
Colour channel: a Vega scheme name (`viridis`, `redblue`), or the stops a ramp or palette runs
through, low end first (`["#c0392b", "#f2f2f2", "#2e75b6"]`). Wins over the theme's ramp.

members.name: reverse
members.documentation: Colour channel: run the scale the other way round.

members.name: mid
members.documentation: Colour channel: the value a diverging scale pivots on, for this chart (the field's `divergingMidpoint`).

members.name: domain
members.documentation: Colour channel: the measure extent the ramp spans, `[low, high]`, in place of the data's.

members.name: bins
members.documentation: Colour channel: quantize a continuous measure into this many bins; `0` keeps the ramp continuous.

members.name: colors
members.documentation: Colour channel: colours bound to values, for this chart (the field's `colors`): `{ "Win": "#2a9d8f" }`.

members.name: title
members.documentation:
The name the channel's axis or key prints, in place of the field's; `null` prints none. A
theme still decides whether a key is titled at all: a name given here renames it where it is.

declarations.name: EncodingValue
declarations.documentation:
An encoding value that allows either a single encoding or an array of

When an array is provided, the assembler folds (unpivots) the specified
fields into a long-form representation with a synthesized key column
(for color/legend) and value column (for the measure axis).

`{ field: <string> }`. This lets callers write `{ x: "weight" }` instead of
`{ x: { field: "weight" } }` to keep simple specs terse (e.g. for demos).

Shorthands are also accepted inside static-series arrays, so
`{ y: ["sales", "profit"] }` expands to `[{ field: "sales" }, { field: "profit" }]`.

members.name: colorActsAsGroup

Treat a discrete `color` field as an axis-grouping field for sizing,
even though the template uses the `color` channel rather than `group`.

not balloon and each sub-lane shrinks as the subgroup count grows.
Used by charts (e.g. boxplot) that dodge by color via an explicit offset.

field. Templates that render `local` (compact) dodge set this to the
per-band max cardinality (`maxPerBand`) so the band is budgeted for only
as many lanes as the busiest band actually uses.

declarations.name: LayoutResult
declarations.documentation:
Phase 1 output: all layout decisions.

LayoutResult is **target-agnostic** — it describes abstract dimensions
and step sizes that any rendering backend can consume.  It is the
backend's responsibility to translate these values into its own
coordinate system:

  subplotWidth / subplotHeight
    The intended data-area (plot area) size in pixels.  This does NOT
    include axis labels, titles, legends, or margins.  Each backend
    must add its own margins/padding around this area.

  xStep / yStep
    Pixel distance per discrete position on each axis.  A backend
    rendering bars should derive bar width from step and stepPadding.
    VL uses `width: {step: N}` natively; ECharts must compute
    explicit barWidth / barCategoryGap.

  stepPadding
    Fraction of each step reserved for inter-category spacing (0–1).
    Usable bar width = step × (1 − stepPadding).

  facet (columns / rows / subplot sizes)
    When faceting is active, the subplot dimensions are already
    divided for the facet grid.  Each backend is responsible for
    facet wrapping (e.g. column-only → wrapped rows), panel
    positioning, header labels, and shared/per-panel axis titles.

Backends should NOT modify LayoutResult.  They read it and translate
to their native format (VL encoding props, ECharts grid/axis config, etc.).
